annotations.title: Find brands paying creators in a niche, with evidence

description: Find brands with recent public proof of paid placement in a niche. Give a niche (for example health and fitness, beauty and skincare, food and beverage) and optionally audience keywords, seed YouTube channels, podcast feeds, or newsletters, and event sponsor pages. The actor reads public YouTube descriptions, podcast show notes, newsletter issues, event sponsor pages, partnership job posts, and brand creator program pages, and returns one row per brand domain (sighting count, last seen date, sources, creators or events sponsored, public contact, recency score) and one row per sighting (brand, domain, source, creator or event, date, evidence link, promo code, placement type, pitch angle). Instagram, TikTok, and the Meta Ad Library are not read. ROW CAP AND PAGING: a call returns at most max_rows rows (default 50, at most 200) as a JSON array in the first content block, and a paging block in the second with total_rows and next_cursor. To get every row, call again with only cursor set to next_cursor until next_cursor is null. A cursor call reads the same finished run's rows, starts no new run, and is not billed again. Input with nothing to run returns one free row whose error_reason starts with input_invalid:. A run that does not succeed is returned as an error with its run ID. Read-only; requires an APIFY_TOKEN; Apify charges per brand row, per sighting row, and per run start.

audience_keywords.description: Optional. More search terms for the audience, one per line or separated by commas, for example "strength training". Each one widens the podcast, newsletter, and (with your key) YouTube channel search. Up to 20. A text field, so a Clay column maps straight in.

cursor.description: Wrapper setting, not sent to the actor. The next_cursor from the previous call's paging block. With a cursor the call starts no run and returns the next page of that run's rows, so nothing is billed again; every other input except max_rows is ignored.

event_calendar.description: Optional. Events whose sponsor or partner page to read, as a JSON list of objects: [{"name": "...", "url": "sponsor page URL", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "city": "...", "audience": "...", "size": "..."}], or one sponsor page URL per line. url is needed; the rest is optional. A dated event inside the window gives dated rows; an undated or upcoming event gives undated rows.

include_brands.description: true or false, default true. One row per brand domain with sighting count, last seen date, sources, creators or events, contact, and recency score. Default true.

include_sightings.description: true or false, default true. One row per sighting with its evidence link, date, promo code, placement type, and pitch angle. Default true.

max_brands_to_check.description: Brands, most sighted first, whose job boards and program pages are checked. Whole number, default 25, at most 200. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 25.

max_channels.description: YouTube channels read per run. Whole number, default 20, at most 100. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 20.

max_charge_usd.description: Optional. The run stops before it would charge more than this.

max_episodes_per_podcast.description: Newest episodes read per show. Whole number, default 8, at most 30. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 8.

max_issues_per_newsletter.description: Newest issues read per newsletter. Whole number, default 8, at most 30. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 8.

max_newsletters.description: Newsletters read per run. Whole number, default 8, at most 50. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 8.

max_podcasts.description: Podcast shows read per run. Whole number, default 15, at most 100. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 15.

max_rows.description: Wrapper setting, not sent to the actor. Rows returned per call: whole number, default 50, at most 200. Reach the rest of the run's rows with cursor.

max_videos_per_channel.description: Newest uploads read per channel (the public feed holds 15). Whole number, default 15, at most 50. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 15.

niche.description: The audience niche, for example "health and fitness", "beauty and skincare", or "food and beverage". Searches for channels, shows, and newsletters use it, and every row carries it. These three niches also start from a list of sources Mamba Labs has read before (turn off with use_niche_presets).

seed_sources.description: Optional. YouTube channel URLs or @handles, podcast RSS feed URLs, or newsletter URLs to read first, one per line or separated by commas. Each is read even beyond the per source limits.

sources.description: Optional. Which sources to run, separated by commas, any of: youtube, podcast, event, newsletter, job_post, program. Empty runs all of them. job_post and program check the brands the other sources found.

use_niche_presets.description: true or false, default true. For health and fitness, beauty and skincare, and food and beverage, also read the channels, shows, newsletters, and event pages Mamba Labs has read before. Default true.

window_days.description: Only sightings from the last N days. Whole number, default 90, at most 365. Sent as text so Clay works. Default 90.
